# Review pack: The vision described in the surah of the star

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/prophets-vision.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the vision, on the identity of the one who taught and the one seen, and on the occasion, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
- This story is drafted with the greatest restraint. It states only what the verses say, names no angel, describes no one, and leaves out 53:6-9, which speak of position and nearness. A scholar should decide whether and how to include them.
- Whether the one who taught (53:5) and the one seen (53:13) are the same, and who they are, is a question the verses leave to interpretation; the draft does not decide it.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the companion, of the teacher and of the one seen, and the occasion of the passage.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The companion who has not strayed  (`#the-companion-has-not-strayed`)

Cited ayat: 53:1-4

> **53:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ وَٱلنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ
>
> **53:2** مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَىٰ
>
> **53:3** وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ
>
> **53:4** إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْىٌ يُوحَىٰ

### Claims

**c1** (53:1): God swears by the star when it falls.

**c2** (53:2): God says that the companion of those addressed has neither strayed nor erred.

**c3** (53:3): He does not speak out of desire.

**c4** (53:4): It is nothing but a revelation that is being revealed.

### One-minute summary

God swears by the star when it falls [c1]. He says that the companion of those addressed has neither strayed nor erred [c2], and that he does not speak out of desire [c3]. It is nothing but a revelation being revealed [c4].

### Complete story

God swears by the star when it falls [c1].

He says that the companion of those addressed has neither strayed nor erred [c2]. He does not speak out of desire [c3]. It is nothing but a revelation that is being revealed [c4].

### Deep study

The passage opens with an oath and then makes a series of statements about the companion [c1][c2][c3]. The last statement says what 'it' is, and does so by the word revelation [c4]. The verse does not say what 'it' refers to [c4].

### Kids mode

God swears by the star when it falls [c1]. God says that the companion has not strayed and has not erred [c2]. He does not speak out of desire [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage separates what is said out of desire from what is revealed [c3][c4]. Another is that it begins by setting the companion's honesty before anything else is said [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the companion is. The verse says 'your companion' and gives no name.
- Not established: what 'it' refers to in 53:4, or whether 'the star when it falls' is a star, a group of stars, or something else; the Arabic word and its verb are read in more than one way.
- Not established: when or where the words were first heard.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the companion and the occasion. Neither is used in the story texts.

## 2. The one who taught  (`#the-one-who-taught`)

Cited ayat: 53:5, 53:10-12

> **53:5** عَلَّمَهُۥ شَدِيدُ ٱلْقُوَىٰ

> **53:10** فَأَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِۦ مَآ أَوْحَىٰ
>
> **53:11** مَا كَذَبَ ٱلْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَىٰٓ
>
> **53:12** أَفَتُمَٰرُونَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَا يَرَىٰ

### Claims

**c1** (53:5): The companion was taught by one who is strong in power.

**c2** (53:10): God revealed to His servant what He revealed.

**c3** (53:11): The heart did not lie about what it saw.

**c4** (53:12): The verse asks the listeners whether they will dispute with him about what he sees.

### One-minute summary

The passage says that the companion was taught by one who is strong in power [c1]. It says that God revealed to His servant what He revealed [c2], that the heart did not lie about what it saw [c3], and asks whether they will dispute with him about what he sees [c4].

### Complete story

The passage says that the companion was taught by one who is strong in power [c1].

It says that God revealed to His servant what He revealed [c2]. The heart did not lie about what it saw [c3]. The verse then asks the listeners whether they will dispute with him about what he sees [c4].

### Deep study

The passage names a teacher only by a quality, strong in power, and does not name him [c1]. It does not say what God revealed, only that He revealed what He revealed [c2]. It speaks of the heart and of what was seen, and of a dispute about what is seen [c3][c4].

### Kids mode

The passage says that the companion was taught by one who is strong in power [c1]. God revealed to His servant what He revealed [c2]. The verses say that his heart did not lie about what it saw [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage treats what was revealed and what was seen as true and asks the listeners not to dispute it [c3][c4]. Another is that it leaves what was revealed unspecified [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the teacher is. The verses give a quality and no name; later readers differ on who is meant, and the draft takes no side.
- Not established: who 'his servant' is, what was revealed to him, or what the heart saw; the verses say 'what He revealed' and 'what it saw'.
- This chapter leaves out 53:6-9, which speak of where the teacher stood and how near he came. They are left out on purpose, because they invite a picture; a scholar should decide whether the page should present them and in what words.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the teacher and of the one who saw. Neither is used in the story texts.

## 3. At the lote tree of the farthest limit  (`#the-farthest-lote-tree`)

Cited ayat: 53:13-18

> **53:13** وَلَقَدْ رَءَاهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ
>
> **53:14** عِندَ سِدْرَةِ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ
>
> **53:15** عِندَهَا جَنَّةُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰٓ
>
> **53:16** إِذْ يَغْشَى ٱلسِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَىٰ
>
> **53:17** مَا زَاغَ ٱلْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَىٰ
>
> **53:18** لَقَدْ رَأَىٰ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰٓ

### Claims

**c1** (53:13): The verse says that he saw him on another descent, a word that can also be read as another occasion.

**c2** (53:14-15): It was at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near which is the garden of refuge.

**c3** (53:16): This was when the lote tree was covered by what covered it.

**c4** (53:17): The sight did not swerve and did not exceed.

**c5** (53:18): He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.

### One-minute summary

The passage says that he saw him on another descent [c1], at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near which is the garden of refuge [c2]. It says that the sight did not swerve and did not exceed [c4], and that he saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord [c5].

### Complete story

The passage says that he saw him on another descent, a word that can also be read as another occasion [c1].

It was at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near which is the garden of refuge [c2]. This was when the lote tree was covered by what covered it [c3].

The sight did not swerve and did not exceed [c4]. He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord [c5].

### Deep study

The passage does not say who is seen; the pronoun is not resolved in the verse [c1]. It names a place by its names, the lote tree of the farthest limit and the garden of refuge [c2]. What covered the lote tree is not said [c3]. The passage closes with what the sight did not do and with what was seen, signs of his Lord [c4][c5].

### Kids mode

The passage says that he saw something on another occasion [c1]. It was at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near the garden of refuge [c2]. He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage describes what was seen as signs of the Lord and not as an end in itself [c5]. Another is that it speaks of a sight that did not swerve and did not exceed [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: whom he saw, or what he saw. The pronoun in 53:13 is not resolved here, and 'the greatest signs' are not listed.
- Not established: what covered the lote tree, where the tree is, or what 'the farthest limit' is a limit of.
- Not established: when this took place or how it relates to any journey; the verses do not say.
- The Arabic word for 'descent' can be read as a descent or as an occasion; the draft gives both.
- This chapter does not describe the one seen or the manner of the sight, and no verse here does.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the one seen and the occasion. Neither is used in the story texts.
